turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt_extrapolation_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns
    process/composition columns (Sb, O, Te, Co, Mg, Sn, Se, Pb, Si, S, Cu,
    Ge, Ni, Bi, Ti, Fe, Zn, In, Zr, Ca, Ag, T) and `target` (the measured zT
    measured at each row's own temperature T (K)).
  - b3_te_zt_extrapolation_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT at 800 K
    was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same
    process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT at 800
K, then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training observations at the highest available temperature (500 K) provide the most relevant anchors for 800 K extrapolation. A composition-space nearest-neighbor match restricted to those 500 K rows therefore ranks the pool. The five strongest matches (and their 500 K zT values) are:

- c043 is identical to the 1.13 PbTe:Sb observation,
- c046 is within L1 \(\approx 0.06\) of the 0.96 PbTe:Sb observation,
- c022 is within L1 \(\approx 0.085\) of the 0.79 PbTe observation,
- c057 is the nearest neighbour (L1 \(\approx 0.28\)) of the 0.68 Pb(Te,Se) observation,
- c051 is within L1 \(\approx 0.032\) of the 0.61 Cu\(_2\)Se observation.

All other pool compositions lie farther from every high-zT 500 K row (or match only low-zT rows). Consequently these five candidates are predicted to retain the highest zT after the temperature is raised to 800 K.

Final: c043, c046, c022, c057, c051
